subject: Private deployment topology alignment - Orchid Health
messages:
From: Alex Benson <alex.benson@orchidhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Nov 2027 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment topology alignment request

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the quick intro on Friday. We're moving into the design phase for a private on-prem deployment of Redwood for inference (control-plane separate from customer data plane) and want to align on topology expectations and handoff artifacts before we lock the purchase order. High-level asks from my side:

- Confirm required north-south egress controls for telemetry and patching.
- Control plane connectivity model (managed vs customer-managed peering).
- Template runbook / checklist for the cutover day.

I've attached a short PDF with our existing datacenter constraints and a rough network diagram. Can we get a 30–45 minute review early next week? We're in PST.

Appreciate it,
Alex
Alex Benson
Head of Infrastructure
Orchid Health
Attachments: orchid_topology_req.pdf (pdf)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Benson <alex.benson@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment topology alignment request

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the diagram. Looping in Jonas (network architecture) and Kimberly (deploy ops) so we can come prepared.

High-level plan for the sync:
1) 15m — Review Orchid's constraints (the PDF) and confirm control/data plane breakpoints.
2) 15m — Align on egress and telemetry channels (what must traverse customer egress vs what Redwood needs outbound).
3) 10m — Handoff artifacts and next steps (runbook, pre-checklist, expected cutover window).

Two quick notes up front:
- We typically recommend a dedicated control-plane subnet that uses encrypted outbound to Redwood-managed endpoints; customer-managed peering (VPC/VPN) is supported if you need no egress to public internet.
- For telemetry (metrics/traces) we offer buffering to the customer side or via a secured push to a Redwood ingest endpoint; we'll propose both in the meeting so you can pick based on audit needs.

I've attached a reference diagram (redwood-ref-diagram-v1.png) and a draft mutual action plan below. Please confirm availability 11/9 or 11/10 between 09:00–12:00 PST and which telemetry option you prefer for the call.

Draft mutual action plan (high-level):
- Week 0: Design review (this meeting).
- Week 1: Network config & access exchange (VPN certs / peering).
- Week 2: Staging deploy (private control-plane + test customer data plane).
- Week 3: Cutover rehearsal and runbook dry-run.

Thanks — I can host a dial-in and send an agenda.

--
Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Attachments: redwood-ref-diagram-v1.png (image/png)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Alex Benson <alex.benson@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 11:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment topology alignment request

Thanks — quick technical notes ahead of the call.

Irene / Alex — I reviewed the attached Orchid diagram. A couple of points we should confirm on the call:
- Control-plane isolation: we recommend a minimal set of control-plane egress flows (auth, metrics, package updates). If Orchid's security team requires zero egress, we can support an air-gapped profile but it increases operational windows for patching.
- Data-plane traffic: customer inference requests and model data remain on-prem and never route to Redwood endpoints. The only optional flows are model syncing and telemetry.
- MTLS and client certs: for peered/VPN models we'll use MTLS with mutual cert rotation — I'll bring our cert rotation doc.

I'll reference our private-deploy runbook during the meeting: https://redwood.internal/ops/runbooks/private-deploy (internal link).

Small ask for Orchid: a CSV with IP ranges for each datacenter and whether NAT egress is allowed. If you can drop that into the Drive folder ahead of the meeting, we can pre-validate ACLs.

On the call we'll propose a concrete egress policy matrix (what goes outbound, what is pulled behind customer NAT) so we can produce a cutover checklist.

- Jonas
Principal Network Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Benson <alex.benson@orchidhealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment topology alignment request

Alex / team — thanks, this is a productive thread. Drafting the cutover checklist and sharing an MVP handoff sheet (attached). Key items we'll want in place before staging:

- Network: ACLs applied, NAT/egress validated, control-plane subnet routable to peering endpoint.
- Identity: Certs provisioned, SSH key handover for bootstrap ops.
- Data: Model sync window scheduled, test vectors agreed, and success criteria defined.
- Observability: Buffering configured (if no outbound allowed) and an ops playbook for replaying buffered telemetry.

Action items for Orchid before staging:
1) Provide datacenter CIDR CSV and NAT allowance flag.
2) Provision a service account for model sync with restricted scope.
3) Schedule a 2-hour staging window; include a rollback runway in the calendar invite.

I've uploaded "MVP-handoff-checklist.xlsx" to the Drive folder and will bring a ready-to-run checklist to the meeting. Proposed review slot: Wed 11/10 10:00–10:45 PST. Does that work?

Attachments: MVP-handoff-checklist.xlsx

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Deploy Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Benson <alex.benson@orchidhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment topology alignment request

Kimberly / team — 10/11 10:00 PST works for us (I'll send a calendar invite). We'll upload the CIDR CSV and confirm NAT allowance by EOD tomorrow. For telemetry, we'll plan to allow outbound to a vetted Redwood endpoint; if anything changes we'll flag it ahead of the staging run.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the review.

Alex
Head of Infrastructure, Orchid Health
